zotLook previews the attachment of the selected Zotero item when you press
**Space**, the way a file manager does. It does not carry a viewer of its own:
it drives the preview panel the system already has — Quick Look on macOS, GNOME
Sushi on Linux, [QuickLook](https://github.com/QL-Win/QuickLook) on Windows — so
whatever those can show, zotLook can show.

![](asset/screenshot.png)

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| **Zotero** | 7 or later. Tested on 7, 8, 9 and 10. |
| **macOS** | 12 (Monterey) or later. Nothing to install; the panel is part of the system. |
| **Linux** | GNOME Sushi. On Debian and Ubuntu: `sudo apt install gnome-sushi`. |
| **Windows** | [QuickLook](https://github.com/QL-Win/QuickLook), running. Its Microsoft Store build and its desktop build both work. |

## Install

1. Download the latest `.xpi` from the
   [releases page](https://github.com/fre-ms/zotLook/releases).
2. In Zotero: **Tools → Add-ons**.
3. Gear icon → **Install Add-on From File…**
4. Pick the file you downloaded, then restart Zotero.

From then on Zotero checks for new versions itself and updates the plugin
without being asked.

::: {.callout-note}
zotLook installs beside Guillaume Chapron's Zotero7QuickLook rather than over
it — the two carry different plugin IDs. If you have both, disable one, or the
Space key will be claimed twice.
:::

## The first minute

Select an item and press **Space**. If the item is a parent rather than an
attachment, zotLook picks one of its attachments — a PDF before an EPUB before
anything else, and you can [change that order](settings.qmd). Press **Space**
again, or **Escape**, to dismiss the preview.

**Shift+Space** previews the item's notes instead, rendered as a page.

**Ctrl+Shift+Space** builds a *contact sheet*: every page of a PDF as a
thumbnail in a scrollable grid. Clicking a page opens it in Zotero's reader at
that page. On a long document the sheet takes a few seconds and says so while it
works.

If the file is stored in the cloud and not on this machine, zotLook downloads it
first rather than reporting that it is missing.

## Annotations are drawn in

Zotero keeps the highlights and notes you make in its reader in its **database**,
not in the PDF file. Previewing the stored file would therefore show an
unmarked document — the thing users asked about most.

zotLook exports a copy with the annotations drawn in and previews that, in the
preview and on the contact sheet alike. Attachments without annotations are
recognised before any work starts, and an export is reused until you add or
change an annotation, so the usual case costs nothing. It can be switched off
under [Settings](settings.qmd).
